chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from 'Umar al-Jurjani, from Muhammad ibn al-'Ala', from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) say: 'Whoever trims his mustache and clips his fingernails on Friday, then says, "In the name of Allah, upon the Sunnah of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad," Allah will record for him, for every hair and every clipping, the freeing of a slave, and he will not be struck by any illness except the illness of death.'
Al-Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: 'And pray six rak'at when the sun is fully extended, until he says, 'And know that the narration has come.'
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual rewards of grooming on Friday in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq, linking the physical act of *fitrah* (grooming) on Friday with spiritual purification, where each clipped hair or nail earns the reward of freeing a slave. The text further prescribes praying six units at sunrise, emphasizing the holistic sanctification of the day through both bodily care and devotional acts, a practice deeply rooted in Shia jurisprudence as a manifestation of following the Sunnah of the Prophet and his Ahl al-Bayt.
